CHAPTER III

RIGHTS AND OBLIGATIONS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms mean: 1. Region is the City of Bukittinggi. 2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the regional government and the regional house of representatives in accordance with the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 3. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Mayor is the Mayor of Bukittinggi. 5. Regional House of Representatives of the City of Bukittinggi, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution as an element of regional government administration. 6. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is a unit that has authority in the field of women's empowerment and family planning. 7. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 8. Customs are permanent patterns of behavior passed down from one generation to another as heritage so that they are strongly integrated with community behavior patterns. 9. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter abbreviated as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own accord and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare as a manifestation of community participation in improving the standard of living and welfare of the community with emphasis on voluntary service. 10. Social Organization is an institution/foundation/social association formed by the community, whether legally established or not, which functions as a means of community participation in carrying out social welfare activities. 11. Empowerment is a process, method and act of providing power and strength so that a person is able to explore potential and positive energy and have an impact on a better quality of life. 12. Woman is every person who is born, recognized by society and registered as a woman. 13. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily, develop themselves and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial (assistance and treatment) protection. 14. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb. 15. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 16. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, or husband and wife and their children, or father and his children, or mother and her children. 17. Household Scope is husband, wife and children, people who have family relations with the husband, wife and children, whether due to blood relations, marriage, breastfeeding, care, and guardianship who reside in the household, and/or people who work to assist the household and reside in that household. 18. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 19. Guardian is a person or entity who in fact exercises parental authority as a parent over a child. 20. Neglected Child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 21. Child with Disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental障碍 that disrupts their growth and development in a normal manner. 22. Toddler is a child aged 1 (one) to 5 (five) years, in the early stage of human development. 23. School-Age Child is a child aged 6 (six) to 18 (eighteen) years. 24. Delinquent Child is a child who behaves deviating from community norms, harming/endangering their own health/safety, disturbing the peace and order of society and family and community life, but is still below the category that can be prosecuted legally/in court. 25. Child Who Is a Victim of Violence is a child who receives mistreatment such as being abused, humiliated physically, mentally and socially. 26. Child in Conflict with the Law is a child who is in conflict with the law and a child who is a victim of a criminal act. 27. Economically Exploited Child is a child who is forced and deceived to be employed by parents or others without payment or with payment. 28. Child Who Is a Victim of Narcotics Abuse is a child who suffers from dependence on narcotics caused by narcotics abuse either by their own will or due to encouragement or coercion by others. 29. Child Trafficking is a criminal act or action that meets one or more elements of recruitment, transportation, transfer of a child using violence or threat of violence, fraud, abduction, confinement, abuse of power, exploitation of vulnerability or debt bondage for the purpose of and/or resulting in exploiting the child. 30. Social Work Profession is a profession based on a framework of science, values and technical skills and can be used as a vehicle in the implementation of social welfare activities. 31. Child Care Center, hereinafter abbreviated as TPA, is a place for guidance and welfare services for children aged 0-5 years whose parents do not have the ability and opportunity in child care, which is possible for playgroup services. 32. Playgroup is a child welfare facility prioritizing play activities and providing pre-school education for children aged 3 years until entering basic education. 33.

Article 9

Protection for women includes:

Article 3

The objectives of this Regional Regulation are:

a. To protect women and children from actions, decisions and policies that violate basic human rights. b. To provide clear responsibilities for the government, community, family, ninik mamak and parents regarding the rights of children and women.

To protect women and children from violence, neglect, exploitation, and trafficking in persons as well as women's rights in the event of divorce. e. CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The protection of women and children, until now, remains something that is widely discussed globally. There are still many, even in the most developed countries, violations of the rights of women and children continue to this moment. The understanding or view of some communities that see women and children as parties of lower status, or being under the domination of men, until now still cannot be completely eliminated.

Realizing this, in line with national development priorities, the Regional Government of Bukittinggi strives to produce local policies formulated within the framework of regional regulations, a guideline or reference in the empowerment and protection of women and children in a more institutionalized manner.

The purposes of formulating this Draft Regional Regulation are as follows:

1. To protect women and children from actions, decisions and policies that violate fundamental human rights.
2. To provide clear responsibility for the government, community, family, ninik mamak, and parents regarding the rights of children and women.
3. To provide clear boundaries regarding the role of mamak to kemenakan and parents to children.
4. To protect women and children from acts of violence, neglect, exploitation, and human trafficking as well as the rights of women in the event of divorce.
5. To contribute to the realization of gender equality and justice in various activities and to improve the welfare of women and children in Bukittinggi City.
6. To organize the structure and institutions of government and customary institutions in efforts to protect women and children.
7. As a guideline in taking policies for the Regional Government and social institutions in matters related to the protection of women and children in Bukittinggi City.
8. To protect women and children domiciled in Bukittinggi City from actions that violate their fundamental rights.
9. To provide guidelines for the role of the Regional Government, community, parents and other parties involved with the interests of women and children.

With the presence of this Regional Regulation as a part of the national legal system concerning the protection and empowerment of women and children, all forms of violations of their rights such as being neglected, exploited, discriminated against and even frequently experiencing domestic violence (KDRT), low quality of life, inability to contribute to the progress of development, can be institutionally eliminated, eradicated in our region.

It can be affirmed that this Regional Regulation will later lay down the basic rules regarding the authority, rights and obligations of government, community and elements involved with children and women, by making local wisdom, customary values and the life views of Minangkabau culture towards women and children as the main philosophical foundation, which can simply be expressed through customary expressions such as "bundo kanduang limpapeh rumah nan gadang", and "anak dipangku kemenakan dibimbing".

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 17

(1) Protection of women and children is carried out in the form of:

a. preventive protection;
b. repressive protection; and
c. postremedial protection.
(2) Preventive protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is implemented through socialization and direction to parents, heads of families, housewives, guardians, teaching/education personnel, expert personnel, caregivers (owners and orphanage staff) and customary law communities regarding their obligations in the protection of women and children.
(3) Repressive protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is implemented through law enforcement by law enforcers to establish and implement legal sanctions against people who violate certain child and women's rights.
(4) Postremedial protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is implemented through assistance efforts in law enforcement by lawyers, psychological guidance by psychologists and/or clergy, and placement of victims in safe houses.

Article 6

Every child has the right:

a. To live, grow, develop and participate appropriately in accordance with human dignity, and to receive protection from acts of violence, exploitation, discrimination and neglect.
b. To have a name as personal identity and citizenship status.
c. To worship according to their religion, think and express themselves in accordance with their level of intelligence and age, under parental guidance.
d. To know their parents, be cared for and raised by their own parents.
e. In the event that for any reason the parents cannot guarantee the child's growth and development, or the child is in a state of neglect, then the child has the right to be cared for or adopted as a foster child or adopted child by others in accordance with the provisions of the applicable laws and regulations.
f. To receive health services and social security in accordance with physical, mental, spiritual, and social needs.
g. To receive education and instruction for the development of their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.
h. To receive protection in educational institutions from sexual crimes and violence committed by educators, educational personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.
i. To receive special and extraordinary education for children with disabilities and children with excellence.
j. To express and have their opinion heard, receive, seek, and provide information in accordance with their level of intelligence and age for their self-development in accordance with the values of decency and propriety.
k. To rest and utilize leisure time, socialize with peers, play, recreate, and create in accordance with their interests, talents, and level of intelligence for self-development.
l. To receive rehabilitation, social assistance and recovery of social welfare standards for children with disabilities.
m. To receive protection from treatment while in the care of parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for care, from discriminatory treatment, exploitation, both economic and sexual, neglect, cruelty, violence, and abuse, injustice and other mistreatment.
n. To be cared for by their own parents, unless there are valid reasons and/or legal rules showing that such separation is in the best interests of the child and is a last resort.
o. In the event of separation between the child and their parents, the child still has the right to:
1. meet directly and maintain personal contact regularly with both parents;
2. receive care, maintenance, education and protection for the growth and development process from both parents in accordance with their abilities, talents and interests;
3. receive financial support from both parents; and
4. receive other children's rights.
p. To receive protection from abuse in political activities, involvement in armed conflicts, involvement in social unrest, involvement in events containing elements of violence, involvement in warfare and sexual crimes.
q. To receive protection from being targets of persecution, torture or imposition of inhumane punishment or sanctions.
r. To obtain freedom in accordance with the law. s. Every child deprived of their liberty has the right to: 1. receive humane treatment and be placed separately from adults;
2. receive legal assistance or other assistance effectively at every stage of applicable legal remedies; and
3. defend themselves and obtain justice before an objective and impartial juvenile court in a closed hearing.
t. Every child who becomes a victim or perpetrator of sexual violence or who is in conflict with the law has the right to confidentiality.
u. To receive legal assistance and other assistance if they become a victim or perpetrator of a criminal act.

Article 27

(1) Every person who knows that a violation of women's and children's rights has occurred is obliged to report the occurrence of such violation to law enforcement.

(2) Every person, blood relatives, clan members, paruik members, tribe members, village members, or nagari members is obliged to report to law enforcement if they know that a violation of women's and children's rights has occurred.

Article 4

Every woman has the right to:

a. Obtain protection from discrimination, exploitation (economic and social), neglect, cruelty, violence, persecution (physical, psychological, and sexual), injustice and other wrongful treatment.
b. Obtain opportunities and rights equal to those of men as human beings, in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social and cultural activities, defense and security and equality in enjoying the results of development.
c. For working women:
1. obtain leave/rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months before the time of childbirth and 1.5 (one and a half) months after childbirth according to the calculation of an obstetrician or midwife, while continuing to receive wages or salary in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations;
2. obtain leave/rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months in case of miscarriage while continuing to receive wages or salary in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations;
3. obtain appropriate opportunity to breastfeed her child if this must be done during working hours, while continuing to receive wages or salary in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.
d. Every married woman has the right to receive material and spiritual support from her husband.
e. Every woman who is left by her husband due to divorce proceedings must be provided material support by her husband until there is a court decision in accordance with the laws and regulations.
f. Every woman has the right to obtain decent work in accordance with her dignity, honor and nature.
g. Obtain knowledge and skills useful for improving self-quality and family welfare.

CHAPTER VI

SYSTEM FOR THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN Article 16

(1) Protection of women and children is implemented by upholding universal values stated in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

(2) Bureaucratic restrictions must not hinder efforts to protect women and children.

(3) Every parent, adoptive parent, guardian, teaching/education personnel, expert personnel, caregiver in orphanages, and leaders of customary law community members must carry out obligations regarding the rights of children they care for and nurture.

(4) Every head of family, head of clan, head of tribe, leader, or other designation of customary law community leader must fulfill their obligations towards women within their family, clan and tribe.

Article 23

(1) Complaint Handling Services for violations of women's and children's rights are carried out by P2TP2A, PPA Units at the District Police, Community Health Centers, Government Hospitals, and Legal Aid Institutions.

(2) P2TP2A is established by the Regional Government.

(3) The P2TP2A management is established by Mayor's Decree with a management term of 2 (two) years.

(4) In carrying out its principal duties and functions, P2TP2A is financed by the Regional Budget or other legitimate sources.

(5) Complaint Handling Services are conducted in the form of:

a. reporters (victims or families, community and/or institutions) come directly, by telephone and/or letter to report acts of violence;
b. reporters are referred by NGOs, social organizations, community or mass media; and
c. in certain cases officers may visit victims (reporters) directly.

CHAPTER V

RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN Article 11

The Regional Government together with the community is obliged and responsible to provide support for facilities and infrastructure in the implementation of the protection of women and children.

CHAPTER IV

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN Article 8

The Regional Government is responsible for the active implementation of protection for women and children.

CHAPTER VIII

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION AGAINST

VIOLATIONS OF THE RIGHTS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 24

(1) Every woman or child who becomes a victim of violations of women's and children's rights is accompanied by a lawyer provided by the regional government in the context of case handling.

(2) The costs of assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) are budgeted in the Regional Budget.

Article 19

(1) The Regional Government is obliged to conduct socialization and education regarding the protection of women and children by involving all elements of customary stakeholders, as well as universities and other community organizations in the Region.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The protection of women and children, until now, remains something that is widely discussed globally. There are still many, even in the most developed countries, violations of the rights of women and children continue to this moment. The understanding or view of some communities that see women and children as parties of lower status, or being under the domination of men, until now still cannot be completely eliminated.

Realizing this, in line with national development priorities, the Regional Government of Bukittinggi strives to produce local policies formulated within the framework of regional regulations, a guideline or reference in the empowerment and protection of women and children in a more institutionalized manner.

The purposes of formulating this Draft Regional Regulation are as follows:

1. To protect women and children from actions, decisions and policies that violate fundamental human rights.
2. To provide clear responsibility for the government, community, family, ninik mamak, and parents regarding the rights of children and women.
3. To provide clear boundaries regarding the role of mamak to kemenakan and parents to children.
4. To protect women and children from acts of violence, neglect, exploitation, and human trafficking as well as the rights of women in the event of divorce.
5. To contribute to the realization of gender equality and justice in various activities and to improve the welfare of women and children in Bukittinggi City.
6. To organize the structure and institutions of government and customary institutions in efforts to protect women and children.
7. As a guideline in taking policies for the Regional Government and social institutions in matters related to the protection of women and children in Bukittinggi City.
8. To protect women and children domiciled in Bukittinggi City from actions that violate their fundamental rights.
9. To provide guidelines for the role of the Regional Government, community, parents and other parties involved with the interests of women and children.

With the presence of this Regional Regulation as a part of the national legal system concerning the protection and empowerment of women and children, all forms of violations of their rights such as being neglected, exploited, discriminated against and even frequently experiencing domestic violence (KDRT), low quality of life, inability to contribute to the progress of development, can be institutionally eliminated, eradicated in our region.

It can be affirmed that this Regional Regulation will later lay down the basic rules regarding the authority, rights and obligations of government, community and elements involved with children and women, by making local wisdom, customary values and the life views of Minangkabau culture towards women and children as the main philosophical foundation, which can simply be expressed through customary expressions such as "bundo kanduang limpapeh rumah nan gadang", and "anak dipangku kemenakan dibimbing".

(1) Every person who knows that a violation of women's and children's rights has occurred is obliged to report the occurrence of such violation to law enforcement.

Article 17

a. preventive protection;
b. repressive protection; and
c. postremedial protection.

Article 6

Every child has the right:

a. To live, grow, develop and participate appropriately in accordance with human dignity, and to receive protection from acts of violence, exploitation, discrimination and neglect.
b. To have a name as personal identity and citizenship status.
c. To worship according to their religion, think and express themselves in accordance with their level of intelligence and age, under parental guidance.
d. To know their parents, be cared for and raised by their own parents.
e. In the event that for any reason the parents cannot guarantee the child's growth and development, or the child is in a state of neglect, then the child has the right to be cared for or adopted as a foster child or adopted child by others in accordance with the provisions of the applicable laws and regulations.
f. To receive health services and social security in accordance with physical, mental, spiritual, and social needs.
g. To receive education and instruction for the development of their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.
h. To receive protection in educational institutions from sexual crimes and violence committed by educators, educational personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.
i. To receive special and extraordinary education for children with disabilities and children with excellence.
j. To express and have their opinion heard, receive, seek, and provide information in accordance with their level of intelligence and age for their self-development in accordance with the values of decency and propriety.
k. To rest and utilize leisure time, socialize with peers, play, recreate, and create in accordance with their interests, talents, and level of intelligence for self-development.
l. To receive rehabilitation, social assistance and recovery of social welfare standards for children with disabilities.
m. To receive protection from treatment while in the care of parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for care, from discriminatory treatment, exploitation, both economic and sexual, neglect, cruelty, violence, and abuse, injustice and other mistreatment.
n. To be cared for by their own parents, unless there are valid reasons and/or legal rules showing that such separation is in the best interests of the child and is a last resort.
o. In the event of separation between the child and their parents, the child still has the right to:
1. meet directly and maintain personal contact regularly with both parents;
2. receive care, maintenance, education and protection for the growth and development process from both parents in accordance with their abilities, talents and interests;
3. receive financial support from both parents; and
4. receive other children's rights.
p. To receive protection from abuse in political activities, involvement in armed conflicts, involvement in social unrest, involvement in events containing elements of violence, involvement in warfare and sexual crimes.
q. To receive protection from being targets of persecution, torture or imposition of inhumane punishment or sanctions.
r. To obtain freedom in accordance with the law. s. Every child deprived of their liberty has the right to: 1. receive humane treatment and be placed separately from adults;
2. receive legal assistance or other assistance effectively at every stage of applicable legal remedies; and
3. defend themselves and obtain justice before an objective and impartial juvenile court in a closed hearing.
t. Every child who becomes a victim or perpetrator of sexual violence or who is in conflict with the law has the right to confidentiality.
u. To receive legal assistance and other assistance if they become a victim or perpetrator of a criminal act.

Article 20

(1) Violations of women's rights, whether in the form of physical, psychological, discriminatory treatment, and exploitation must receive legal protection and be prosecuted legally.

(2) In addition to the application of state law as referred to in paragraph (1), perpetrators of violations of women's rights may be subject to sanctions according to customs that live and develop in the community.

Article 22

(1) Violations of children's rights, whether in physical, psychological form, discriminatory treatment, and exploitation must receive legal protection and be prosecuted legally.

(2) In addition to the application of state law as referred to in paragraph (1), perpetrators of violations of women's rights may be subject to sanctions according to customary law that lives and develops in the midst of society.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 4

Every woman has the right to:

a. Obtain protection from discrimination, exploitation (economic and social), neglect, cruelty, violence, persecution (physical, psychological, and sexual), injustice and other wrongful treatment.
b. Obtain opportunities and rights equal to those of men as human beings, in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social and cultural activities, defense and security and equality in enjoying the results of development.
c. For working women:
1. obtain leave/rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months before the time of childbirth and 1.5 (one and a half) months after childbirth according to the calculation of an obstetrician or midwife, while continuing to receive wages or salary in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations;
2. obtain leave/rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months in case of miscarriage while continuing to receive wages or salary in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations;
3. obtain appropriate opportunity to breastfeed her child if this must be done during working hours, while continuing to receive wages or salary in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.
d. Every married woman has the right to receive material and spiritual support from her husband.
e. Every woman who is left by her husband due to divorce proceedings must be provided material support by her husband until there is a court decision in accordance with the laws and regulations.
f. Every woman has the right to obtain decent work in accordance with her dignity, honor and nature.
g. Obtain knowledge and skills useful for improving self-quality and family welfare.

Neglected Child is a child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social. 21. Child with Disability is a child who experiences physical and/or mental障碍 that disrupts their growth and development in a normal manner. 22. Toddler is a child aged 1 (one) to 5 (five) years, in the early stage of human development. 23. School-Age Child is a child aged 6 (six) to 18 (eighteen) years. 24. Delinquent Child is a child who behaves deviating from community norms, harming/endangering their own health/safety, disturbing the peace and order of society and family and community life, but is still below the category that can be prosecuted legally/in court. 25. Child Who Is a Victim of Violence is a child who receives mistreatment such as being abused, humiliated physically, mentally and socially. 26. Child in Conflict with the Law is a child who is in conflict with the law and a child who is a victim of a criminal act. 27. Economically Exploited Child is a child who is forced and deceived to be employed by parents or others without payment or with payment. 28. Child Who Is a Victim of Narcotics Abuse is a child who suffers from dependence on narcotics caused by narcotics abuse either by their own will or due to encouragement or coercion by others. 29. Child Trafficking is a criminal act or action that meets one or more elements of recruitment, transportation, transfer of a child using violence or threat of violence, fraud, abduction, confinement, abuse of power, exploitation of vulnerability or debt bondage for the purpose of and/or resulting in exploiting the child. 30. Social Work Profession is a profession based on a framework of science, values and technical skills and can be used as a vehicle in the implementation of social welfare activities. 31. Child Care Center, hereinafter abbreviated as TPA, is a place for guidance and welfare services for children aged 0-5 years whose parents do not have the ability and opportunity in child care, which is possible for playgroup services. 32. Playgroup is a child welfare facility prioritizing play activities and providing pre-school education for children aged 3 years until entering basic education. 33.

Article 4

Every woman has the right to:

a. Obtain protection from discrimination, exploitation (economic and social), neglect, cruelty, violence, persecution (physical, psychological, and sexual), injustice and other wrongful treatment.
b. Obtain opportunities and rights equal to those of men as human beings, in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social and cultural activities, defense and security and equality in enjoying the results of development.
c. For working women:
1. obtain leave/rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months before the time of childbirth and 1.5 (one and a half) months after childbirth according to the calculation of an obstetrician or midwife, while continuing to receive wages or salary in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations;
2. obtain leave/rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months in case of miscarriage while continuing to receive wages or salary in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations;
3. obtain appropriate opportunity to breastfeed her child if this must be done during working hours, while continuing to receive wages or salary in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.
d. Every married woman has the right to receive material and spiritual support from her husband.
e. Every woman who is left by her husband due to divorce proceedings must be provided material support by her husband until there is a court decision in accordance with the laws and regulations.
f. Every woman has the right to obtain decent work in accordance with her dignity, honor and nature.
g. Obtain knowledge and skills useful for improving self-quality and family welfare.

Article 34

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The protection of women and children, until now, remains something that is widely discussed globally. There are still many, even in the most developed countries, violations of the rights of women and children continue to this moment. The understanding or view of some communities that see women and children as parties of lower status, or being under the domination of men, until now still cannot be completely eliminated.

Realizing this, in line with national development priorities, the Regional Government of Bukittinggi strives to produce local policies formulated within the framework of regional regulations, a guideline or reference in the empowerment and protection of women and children in a more institutionalized manner.

The purposes of formulating this Draft Regional Regulation are as follows:

1. To protect women and children from actions, decisions and policies that violate fundamental human rights.
2. To provide clear responsibility for the government, community, family, ninik mamak, and parents regarding the rights of children and women.
3. To provide clear boundaries regarding the role of mamak to kemenakan and parents to children.
4. To protect women and children from acts of violence, neglect, exploitation, and human trafficking as well as the rights of women in the event of divorce.
5. To contribute to the realization of gender equality and justice in various activities and to improve the welfare of women and children in Bukittinggi City.
6. To organize the structure and institutions of government and customary institutions in efforts to protect women and children.
7. As a guideline in taking policies for the Regional Government and social institutions in matters related to the protection of women and children in Bukittinggi City.
8. To protect women and children domiciled in Bukittinggi City from actions that violate their fundamental rights.
9. To provide guidelines for the role of the Regional Government, community, parents and other parties involved with the interests of women and children.

With the presence of this Regional Regulation as a part of the national legal system concerning the protection and empowerment of women and children, all forms of violations of their rights such as being neglected, exploited, discriminated against and even frequently experiencing domestic violence (KDRT), low quality of life, inability to contribute to the progress of development, can be institutionally eliminated, eradicated in our region.

It can be affirmed that this Regional Regulation will later lay down the basic rules regarding the authority, rights and obligations of government, community and elements involved with children and women, by making local wisdom, customary values and the life views of Minangkabau culture towards women and children as the main philosophical foundation, which can simply be expressed through customary expressions such as "bundo kanduang limpapeh rumah nan gadang", and "anak dipangku kemenakan dibimbing".

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 27

(1) Every person who knows that a violation of women's and children's rights has occurred is obliged to report the occurrence of such violation to law enforcement.

(2) Every person, blood relatives, clan members, paruik members, tribe members, village members, or nagari members is obliged to report to law enforcement if they know that a violation of women's and children's rights has occurred.

Article 17

(1) Protection of women and children is carried out in the form of:

a. preventive protection;
b. repressive protection; and
c. postremedial protection.
(2) Preventive protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is implemented through socialization and direction to parents, heads of families, housewives, guardians, teaching/education personnel, expert personnel, caregivers (owners and orphanage staff) and customary law communities regarding their obligations in the protection of women and children.
(3) Repressive protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is implemented through law enforcement by law enforcers to establish and implement legal sanctions against people who violate certain child and women's rights.
(4) Postremedial protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is implemented through assistance efforts in law enforcement by lawyers, psychological guidance by psychologists and/or clergy, and placement of victims in safe houses.

Article 9

Protection for women includes:

a. Conducting socialization, education and anti-violence against women campaigns by actively involving all Regional Government Work Units, work partners and the community.
b. Ensuring gender mainstreaming programs in every Regional Government Work Unit, to guarantee equality between men and women, as reflected in the Budget Plan of Regional Government Work Units.
c. Conducting early detection of cases of violence against women.
d. Providing service facilities for victims of violence against women, both services for physical victims and psychological services for victims, through the improvement of special facilities and facilities at Hospitals and at P2TP2A.
e. Requiring all Hospitals to be willing to accept women victims of violence for post-mortem examination and to undergo medical treatment.
f. Granting women's rights in accordance with their dignity as women.
g. Protecting women workers from acts of discrimination, exploitation and violence.
h. Requiring the provision of special facilities and infrastructure for women according to criteria, in every government building, private office and other public facilities.
i. Requiring the provision of lactation room facilities for government buildings that provide public services and other public facility places such as malls, supermarkets, doctor's practices and the like.

CHAPTER VI

SYSTEM FOR THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN Article 16

(1) Protection of women and children is implemented by upholding universal values stated in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

(2) Bureaucratic restrictions must not hinder efforts to protect women and children.

(3) Every parent, adoptive parent, guardian, teaching/education personnel, expert personnel, caregiver in orphanages, and leaders of customary law community members must carry out obligations regarding the rights of children they care for and nurture.

(4) Every head of family, head of clan, head of tribe, leader, or other designation of customary law community leader must fulfill their obligations towards women within their family, clan and tribe.

CHAPTER V

RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN Article 11

The Regional Government together with the community is obliged and responsible to provide support for facilities and infrastructure in the implementation of the protection of women and children.

Article 6

Every child has the right:

a. To live, grow, develop and participate appropriately in accordance with human dignity, and to receive protection from acts of violence, exploitation, discrimination and neglect.
b. To have a name as personal identity and citizenship status.
c. To worship according to their religion, think and express themselves in accordance with their level of intelligence and age, under parental guidance.
d. To know their parents, be cared for and raised by their own parents.
e. In the event that for any reason the parents cannot guarantee the child's growth and development, or the child is in a state of neglect, then the child has the right to be cared for or adopted as a foster child or adopted child by others in accordance with the provisions of the applicable laws and regulations.
f. To receive health services and social security in accordance with physical, mental, spiritual, and social needs.
g. To receive education and instruction for the development of their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.
h. To receive protection in educational institutions from sexual crimes and violence committed by educators, educational personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.
i. To receive special and extraordinary education for children with disabilities and children with excellence.
j. To express and have their opinion heard, receive, seek, and provide information in accordance with their level of intelligence and age for their self-development in accordance with the values of decency and propriety.
k. To rest and utilize leisure time, socialize with peers, play, recreate, and create in accordance with their interests, talents, and level of intelligence for self-development.
l. To receive rehabilitation, social assistance and recovery of social welfare standards for children with disabilities.
m. To receive protection from treatment while in the care of parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for care, from discriminatory treatment, exploitation, both economic and sexual, neglect, cruelty, violence, and abuse, injustice and other mistreatment.
n. To be cared for by their own parents, unless there are valid reasons and/or legal rules showing that such separation is in the best interests of the child and is a last resort.
o. In the event of separation between the child and their parents, the child still has the right to:
1. meet directly and maintain personal contact regularly with both parents;
2. receive care, maintenance, education and protection for the growth and development process from both parents in accordance with their abilities, talents and interests;
3. receive financial support from both parents; and
4. receive other children's rights.
p. To receive protection from abuse in political activities, involvement in armed conflicts, involvement in social unrest, involvement in events containing elements of violence, involvement in warfare and sexual crimes.
q. To receive protection from being targets of persecution, torture or imposition of inhumane punishment or sanctions.
r. To obtain freedom in accordance with the law. s. Every child deprived of their liberty has the right to: 1. receive humane treatment and be placed separately from adults;
2. receive legal assistance or other assistance effectively at every stage of applicable legal remedies; and
3. defend themselves and obtain justice before an objective and impartial juvenile court in a closed hearing.
t. Every child who becomes a victim or perpetrator of sexual violence or who is in conflict with the law has the right to confidentiality.
u. To receive legal assistance and other assistance if they become a victim or perpetrator of a criminal act.

The understanding or view of some communities that see women and children as parties of lower status, or being under the domination of men, until now still cannot be completely eliminated.

Realizing this, in line with national development priorities, the Regional Government of Bukittinggi strives to produce local policies formulated within the framework of regional regulations, a guideline or reference in the empowerment and protection of women and children in a more institutionalized manner.

The purposes of formulating this Draft Regional Regulation are as follows:

1. To protect women and children from actions, decisions and policies that violate fundamental human rights.
2. To provide clear responsibility for the government, community, family, ninik mamak, and parents regarding the rights of children and women.
3. To provide clear boundaries regarding the role of mamak to kemenakan and parents to children.
4. To protect women and children from acts of violence, neglect, exploitation, and human trafficking as well as the rights of women in the event of divorce.
5. To contribute to the realization of gender equality and justice in various activities and to improve the welfare of women and children in Bukittinggi City.
6. To organize the structure and institutions of government and customary institutions in efforts to protect women and children.
7. As a guideline in taking policies for the Regional Government and social institutions in matters related to the protection of women and children in Bukittinggi City.
8. To protect women and children domiciled in Bukittinggi City from actions that violate their fundamental rights.
9. To provide guidelines for the role of the Regional Government, community, parents and other parties involved with the interests of women and children.

With the presence of this Regional Regulation as a part of the national legal system concerning the protection and empowerment of women and children, all forms of violations of their rights such as being neglected, exploited, discriminated against and even frequently experiencing domestic violence (KDRT), low quality of life, inability to contribute to the progress of development, can be institutionally eliminated, eradicated in our region.

It can be affirmed that this Regional Regulation will later lay down the basic rules regarding the authority, rights and obligations of government, community and elements involved with children and women, by making local wisdom, customary values and the life views of Minangkabau culture towards women and children as the main philosophical foundation, which can simply be expressed through customary expressions such as "bundo kanduang limpapeh rumah nan gadang", and "anak dipangku kemenakan dibimbing".

CHAPTER IV

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN Article 8

The Regional Government is responsible for the active implementation of protection for women and children.

CHAPTER VIII

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION AGAINST

VIOLATIONS OF THE RIGHTS OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 23

(1) Complaint Handling Services for violations of women's and children's rights are carried out by P2TP2A, PPA Units at the District Police, Community Health Centers, Government Hospitals, and Legal Aid Institutions.

(2) P2TP2A is established by the Regional Government.

(3) The P2TP2A management is established by Mayor's Decree with a management term of 2 (two) years.

(4) In carrying out its principal duties and functions, P2TP2A is financed by the Regional Budget or other legitimate sources.

(5) Complaint Handling Services are conducted in the form of:

a. reporters (victims or families, community and/or institutions) come directly, by telephone and/or letter to report acts of violence;
b. reporters are referred by NGOs, social organizations, community or mass media; and
c. in certain cases officers may visit victims (reporters) directly.

CHAPTER VII

IMPLEMENTATION OF SOCIALIZATION FOR THE PROTECTION OF

WOMEN AND CHILDREN

Article 18

Protection of women and children must be implemented by parents, families, relatives, guardians, caregivers, teachers, the Regional Government, and customary law communities in the Region.

Article 27

(1) Every person who knows that a violation of women's and children's rights has occurred is obliged to report the occurrence of such violation to law enforcement.

(2) Every person, blood relatives, clan members, paruik members, tribe members, village members, or nagari members is obliged to report to law enforcement if they know that a violation of women's and children's rights has occurred.

Article 2

The Implementation of Protection of Women and Children is based on:

(1) Pancasila and the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia.
(2) Basic principles of children's rights, including non-discrimination, best interests of the child, right to life, survival and development, and respect for the views of the child.
(3) Universal teachings which state that women and children are very important parts in the context of the sustainability of a nation, not only viewed in religious norms, but in their implementation constitute human resources in the development of a nation.
(4) The worldview and philosophy of Minangkabau customs set forth in the teachings of Adat Basandi Syarak, Syarak Basandi Kitabullah; Syarak Mangato Adat Mamakai, Alam Takambang Jadi Guru, and Anak dipangku kamanakan dibimbiang, urang kampuang dipatenggangkan.

Article 9

Protection for women includes:

a. Conducting socialization, education and anti-violence against women campaigns by actively involving all Regional Government Work Units, work partners and the community.
b. Ensuring gender mainstreaming programs in every Regional Government Work Unit, to guarantee equality between men and women, as reflected in the Budget Plan of Regional Government Work Units.
c. Conducting early detection of cases of violence against women.
d. Providing service facilities for victims of violence against women, both services for physical victims and psychological services for victims, through the improvement of special facilities and facilities at Hospitals and at P2TP2A.
e. Requiring all Hospitals to be willing to accept women victims of violence for post-mortem examination and to undergo medical treatment.
f. Granting women's rights in accordance with their dignity as women.
g. Protecting women workers from acts of discrimination, exploitation and violence.
h. Requiring the provision of special facilities and infrastructure for women according to criteria, in every government building, private office and other public facilities.
i. Requiring the provision of lactation room facilities for government buildings that provide public services and other public facility places such as malls, supermarkets, doctor's practices and the like.

CHAPTER IX

IMPLEMENTATION OF HANDLING VICTIMS OF VIOLATIONS OF WOMEN'S AND CHILDREN'S RIGHTS

Article 15

Families, caregivers, institutions and customary institutions must play an active role in providing the rights of women and children in accordance with religious and customary norms and applicable statutory regulations.

Article 6

Every child has the right:

a. To live, grow, develop and participate appropriately in accordance with human dignity, and to receive protection from acts of violence, exploitation, discrimination and neglect.
b. To have a name as personal identity and citizenship status.
c. To worship according to their religion, think and express themselves in accordance with their level of intelligence and age, under parental guidance.
d. To know their parents, be cared for and raised by their own parents.
e. In the event that for any reason the parents cannot guarantee the child's growth and development, or the child is in a state of neglect, then the child has the right to be cared for or adopted as a foster child or adopted child by others in accordance with the provisions of the applicable laws and regulations.
f. To receive health services and social security in accordance with physical, mental, spiritual, and social needs.
g. To receive education and instruction for the development of their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.
h. To receive protection in educational institutions from sexual crimes and violence committed by educators, educational personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.
i. To receive special and extraordinary education for children with disabilities and children with excellence.
j. To express and have their opinion heard, receive, seek, and provide information in accordance with their level of intelligence and age for their self-development in accordance with the values of decency and propriety.
k. To rest and utilize leisure time, socialize with peers, play, recreate, and create in accordance with their interests, talents, and level of intelligence for self-development.
l. To receive rehabilitation, social assistance and recovery of social welfare standards for children with disabilities.
m. To receive protection from treatment while in the care of parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for care, from discriminatory treatment, exploitation, both economic and sexual, neglect, cruelty, violence, and abuse, injustice and other mistreatment.
n. To be cared for by their own parents, unless there are valid reasons and/or legal rules showing that such separation is in the best interests of the child and is a last resort.
o. In the event of separation between the child and their parents, the child still has the right to:
1. meet directly and maintain personal contact regularly with both parents;
2. receive care, maintenance, education and protection for the growth and development process from both parents in accordance with their abilities, talents and interests;
3. receive financial support from both parents; and
4. receive other children's rights.
p. To receive protection from abuse in political activities, involvement in armed conflicts, involvement in social unrest, involvement in events containing elements of violence, involvement in warfare and sexual crimes.
q. To receive protection from being targets of persecution, torture or imposition of inhumane punishment or sanctions.
r. To obtain freedom in accordance with the law. s. Every child deprived of their liberty has the right to: 1. receive humane treatment and be placed separately from adults;
2. receive legal assistance or other assistance effectively at every stage of applicable legal remedies; and
3. defend themselves and obtain justice before an objective and impartial juvenile court in a closed hearing.
t. Every child who becomes a victim or perpetrator of sexual violence or who is in conflict with the law has the right to confidentiality.
u. To receive legal assistance and other assistance if they become a victim or perpetrator of a criminal act.

Article 4

Every woman has the right to:

a. Obtain protection from discrimination, exploitation (economic and social), neglect, cruelty, violence, persecution (physical, psychological, and sexual), injustice and other wrongful treatment.
b. Obtain opportunities and rights equal to those of men as human beings, in order to be able to play a role and participate in political, economic, social and cultural activities, defense and security and equality in enjoying the results of development.
c. For working women:
1. obtain leave/rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months before the time of childbirth and 1.5 (one and a half) months after childbirth according to the calculation of an obstetrician or midwife, while continuing to receive wages or salary in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations;
2. obtain leave/rest for 1.5 (one and a half) months in case of miscarriage while continuing to receive wages or salary in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations;
3. obtain appropriate opportunity to breastfeed her child if this must be done during working hours, while continuing to receive wages or salary in accordance with the applicable laws and regulations.
d. Every married woman has the right to receive material and spiritual support from her husband.
e. Every woman who is left by her husband due to divorce proceedings must be provided material support by her husband until there is a court decision in accordance with the laws and regulations.
f. Every woman has the right to obtain decent work in accordance with her dignity, honor and nature.
g. Obtain knowledge and skills useful for improving self-quality and family welfare.

Article 19

(1) The Regional Government is obliged to conduct socialization and education regarding the protection of women and children by involving all elements of customary stakeholders, as well as universities and other community organizations in the Region.

(2) Socialization and education as referred to in paragraph (1) is carried out through the implementation of legal counseling, both with methods of lectures, discussions, pamphlets, films, theatre, randai, saluang, rabab, and other traditional arts.

(3) Financing of programs and activities for socialization and education on the protection of women and children is budgeted in the APBD every year in accordance with the region's financial capacity and statutory regulations.

Article 32

(1) To assist the smooth implementation of the duties of the KLA Task Force, a Secretariat is established.

(2) The Secretariat as referred to in paragraph (1) is tasked with providing technical and administrative support to the KLA Task Force.

(3) The KLA Task Force is domiciled at the Regional Apparatus Organization (SKPD) that oversees women's empowerment, family planning and child protection affairs.

(4) The establishment and membership of the KLA Task Force are stipulated by Mayor's Decree.

Article 22

(1) Violations of children's rights, whether in physical, psychological form, discriminatory treatment, and exploitation must receive legal protection and be prosecuted legally.

(2) In addition to the application of state law as referred to in paragraph (1), perpetrators of violations of women's rights may be subject to sanctions according to customary law that lives and develops in the midst of society.

Article 20

(1) Violations of women's rights, whether in the form of physical, psychological, discriminatory treatment, and exploitation must receive legal protection and be prosecuted legally.

(2) In addition to the application of state law as referred to in paragraph (1), perpetrators of violations of women's rights may be subject to sanctions according to customs that live and develop in the community.

Child Who Is a Victim of Narcotics Abuse is a child who suffers from dependence on narcotics caused by narcotics abuse either by their own will or due to encouragement or coercion by others. 29. Child Trafficking is a criminal act or action that meets one or more elements of recruitment, transportation, transfer of a child using violence or threat of violence, fraud, abduction, confinement, abuse of power, exploitation of vulnerability or debt bondage for the purpose of and/or resulting in exploiting the child. 30. Social Work Profession is a profession based on a framework of science, values and technical skills and can be used as a vehicle in the implementation of social welfare activities. 31. Child Care Center, hereinafter abbreviated as TPA, is a place for guidance and welfare services for children aged 0-5 years whose parents do not have the ability and opportunity in child care, which is possible for playgroup services. 32. Playgroup is a child welfare facility prioritizing play activities and providing pre-school education for children aged 3 years until entering basic education. 33.

Marriage is a physical and spiritual bond between a man and a woman as husband and wife with the aim of forming a happy and lasting family (household) based on the One Supreme God. 34. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 35. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological aspects that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom. 36. Violence Against Women is any action based on gender differences that results or may result in misery or suffering of women, physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom arbitrarily, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life. 37. Violence Against Children is acts of violence physically, sexually, emotional abuse and neglect of children as well as acts of exploitation and discrimination against children that make children sick physically and/or psychologically, depressed, emotionally underdeveloped, feeling marginalized and losing self-confidence. 38. Domestic Violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, psychologically and/or household neglect including threats to commit acts, coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the household scope. 39. Victim of Domestic Violence is a person who experiences violence and/or threat of violence within the household scope. 40. Divorce is the release of the marriage bond by the husband by uttering certain words such as "I have divorced you". 41. Integrated Service Center for Women and Child Empowerment Saayun Salangkah, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A Saayun Salangkah, is one form of service facility for women and children in efforts to fulfill information and needs in the fields of education, health, economy, politics and law, protection and handling of violence and trafficking against women and children in the City of Bukittinggi. 42. Child-Friendly City, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of government, community and business world that is comprehensively and sustainably planned in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights. 43. Child-Friendly City Task Force, hereinafter abbreviated as Gugus Tugas KLA, is a coordinative institution at the city level that coordinates policies, programs and activities to realize KLA.

CHAPTER V

RESPONSIBILITY FOR THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN Article 11

The Regional Government together with the community is obliged and responsible to provide support for facilities and infrastructure in the implementation of the protection of women and children.

Article 3

The objectives of this Regional Regulation are:

a. To protect women and children from actions, decisions and policies that violate basic human rights. b. To provide clear responsibilities for the government, community, family, ninik mamak and parents regarding the rights of children and women.
c. To provide clear boundaries regarding the role of mamak to kemenakan and parents to children. d. To protect women and children from violence, neglect, exploitation, and trafficking in persons as well as women's rights in the event of divorce. e. To contribute to the realization of gender equality and justice in various activities and to improve the welfare of women and children in the Region.
f. To organize government structures and institutions and customary institutions in efforts to protect women and children.
g. As a guideline in making policies for the Regional Government and social institutions in matters relating to the protection of women and children in the Region.
h. To protect women and children domiciled in the Region from actions that violate their basic rights.
i. To provide guidance on the role of the Regional Government, community, parents and other parties dealing with the interests of women and children.

Article 9

Protection for women includes:

a. Conducting socialization, education and anti-violence against women campaigns by actively involving all Regional Government Work Units, work partners and the community.
b. Ensuring gender mainstreaming programs in every Regional Government Work Unit, to guarantee equality between men and women, as reflected in the Budget Plan of Regional Government Work Units.
c. Conducting early detection of cases of violence against women.
d. Providing service facilities for victims of violence against women, both services for physical victims and psychological services for victims, through the improvement of special facilities and facilities at Hospitals and at P2TP2A.
e. Requiring all Hospitals to be willing to accept women victims of violence for post-mortem examination and to undergo medical treatment.
f. Granting women's rights in accordance with their dignity as women.
g. Protecting women workers from acts of discrimination, exploitation and violence.
h. Requiring the provision of special facilities and infrastructure for women according to criteria, in every government building, private office and other public facilities.
i. Requiring the provision of lactation room facilities for government buildings that provide public services and other public facility places such as malls, supermarkets, doctor's practices and the like.

CHAPTER VI

SYSTEM FOR THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN Article 16

(1) Protection of women and children is implemented by upholding universal values stated in the Universal Declaration of Human Rights.

(2) Bureaucratic restrictions must not hinder efforts to protect women and children.

(3) Every parent, adoptive parent, guardian, teaching/education personnel, expert personnel, caregiver in orphanages, and leaders of customary law community members must carry out obligations regarding the rights of children they care for and nurture.

(4) Every head of family, head of clan, head of tribe, leader, or other designation of customary law community leader must fulfill their obligations towards women within their family, clan and tribe.

Article 6

Every child has the right:

a. To live, grow, develop and participate appropriately in accordance with human dignity, and to receive protection from acts of violence, exploitation, discrimination and neglect.
b. To have a name as personal identity and citizenship status.
c. To worship according to their religion, think and express themselves in accordance with their level of intelligence and age, under parental guidance.
d. To know their parents, be cared for and raised by their own parents.
e. In the event that for any reason the parents cannot guarantee the child's growth and development, or the child is in a state of neglect, then the child has the right to be cared for or adopted as a foster child or adopted child by others in accordance with the provisions of the applicable laws and regulations.
f. To receive health services and social security in accordance with physical, mental, spiritual, and social needs.
g. To receive education and instruction for the development of their personality and level of intelligence in accordance with their interests and talents.
h. To receive protection in educational institutions from sexual crimes and violence committed by educators, educational personnel, fellow students, and/or other parties.
i. To receive special and extraordinary education for children with disabilities and children with excellence.
j. To express and have their opinion heard, receive, seek, and provide information in accordance with their level of intelligence and age for their self-development in accordance with the values of decency and propriety.
k. To rest and utilize leisure time, socialize with peers, play, recreate, and create in accordance with their interests, talents, and level of intelligence for self-development.
l. To receive rehabilitation, social assistance and recovery of social welfare standards for children with disabilities.
m. To receive protection from treatment while in the care of parents, guardians, or any other party responsible for care, from discriminatory treatment, exploitation, both economic and sexual, neglect, cruelty, violence, and abuse, injustice and other mistreatment.
n. To be cared for by their own parents, unless there are valid reasons and/or legal rules showing that such separation is in the best interests of the child and is a last resort.
o. In the event of separation between the child and their parents, the child still has the right to:
1. meet directly and maintain personal contact regularly with both parents;
2. receive care, maintenance, education and protection for the growth and development process from both parents in accordance with their abilities, talents and interests;
3. receive financial support from both parents; and
4. receive other children's rights.
p. To receive protection from abuse in political activities, involvement in armed conflicts, involvement in social unrest, involvement in events containing elements of violence, involvement in warfare and sexual crimes.
q. To receive protection from being targets of persecution, torture or imposition of inhumane punishment or sanctions.
r. To obtain freedom in accordance with the law. s. Every child deprived of their liberty has the right to: 1. receive humane treatment and be placed separately from adults;
2. receive legal assistance or other assistance effectively at every stage of applicable legal remedies; and
3. defend themselves and obtain justice before an objective and impartial juvenile court in a closed hearing.
t. Every child who becomes a victim or perpetrator of sexual violence or who is in conflict with the law has the right to confidentiality.
u. To receive legal assistance and other assistance if they become a victim or perpetrator of a criminal act.

Article 17

(1) Protection of women and children is carried out in the form of:

a. preventive protection;
b. repressive protection; and
c. postremedial protection.
(2) Preventive protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter a is implemented through socialization and direction to parents, heads of families, housewives, guardians, teaching/education personnel, expert personnel, caregivers (owners and orphanage staff) and customary law communities regarding their obligations in the protection of women and children.
(3) Repressive protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter b is implemented through law enforcement by law enforcers to establish and implement legal sanctions against people who violate certain child and women's rights.
(4) Postremedial protection as referred to in paragraph (1) letter c is implemented through assistance efforts in law enforcement by lawyers, psychological guidance by psychologists and/or clergy, and placement of victims in safe houses.

Article 24

(1) Every woman or child who becomes a victim of violations of women's and children's rights is accompanied by a lawyer provided by the regional government in the context of case handling.

(2) The costs of assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) are budgeted in the Regional Budget.

Article 32

(1) To assist the smooth implementation of the duties of the KLA Task Force, a Secretariat is established.

(2) The Secretariat as referred to in paragraph (1) is tasked with providing technical and administrative support to the KLA Task Force.

(3) The KLA Task Force is domiciled at the Regional Apparatus Organization (SKPD) that oversees women's empowerment, family planning and child protection affairs.

(4) The establishment and membership of the KLA Task Force are stipulated by Mayor's Decree.

Article 14

Families, caregivers, institutions, and customary institutions have the right to take action towards women and children in the context of implementing education, embracing religion, skills development, moral and ethical development, as well as entrepreneurship development for women and children in accordance with religious and customary norms.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL

The protection of women and children, until now, remains something that is widely discussed globally. There are still many, even in the most developed countries, violations of the rights of women and children continue to this moment. The understanding or view of some communities that see women and children as parties of lower status, or being under the domination of men, until now still cannot be completely eliminated.

Realizing this, in line with national development priorities, the Regional Government of Bukittinggi strives to produce local policies formulated within the framework of regional regulations, a guideline or reference in the empowerment and protection of women and children in a more institutionalized manner.

The purposes of formulating this Draft Regional Regulation are as follows:

1. To protect women and children from actions, decisions and policies that violate fundamental human rights.
2. To provide clear responsibility for the government, community, family, ninik mamak, and parents regarding the rights of children and women.
3. To provide clear boundaries regarding the role of mamak to kemenakan and parents to children.
4. To protect women and children from acts of violence, neglect, exploitation, and human trafficking as well as the rights of women in the event of divorce.
5. To contribute to the realization of gender equality and justice in various activities and to improve the welfare of women and children in Bukittinggi City.
6. To organize the structure and institutions of government and customary institutions in efforts to protect women and children.
7. As a guideline in taking policies for the Regional Government and social institutions in matters related to the protection of women and children in Bukittinggi City.
8. To protect women and children domiciled in Bukittinggi City from actions that violate their fundamental rights.
9. To provide guidelines for the role of the Regional Government, community, parents and other parties involved with the interests of women and children.

With the presence of this Regional Regulation as a part of the national legal system concerning the protection and empowerment of women and children, all forms of violations of their rights such as being neglected, exploited, discriminated against and even frequently experiencing domestic violence (KDRT), low quality of life, inability to contribute to the progress of development, can be institutionally eliminated, eradicated in our region.

It can be affirmed that this Regional Regulation will later lay down the basic rules regarding the authority, rights and obligations of government, community and elements involved with children and women, by making local wisdom, customary values and the life views of Minangkabau culture towards women and children as the main philosophical foundation, which can simply be expressed through customary expressions such as "bundo kanduang limpapeh rumah nan gadang", and "anak dipangku kemenakan dibimbing".

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms mean: 1. Region is the City of Bukittinggi. 2. Regional Government is the administration of governmental affairs by the regional government and the regional house of representatives in accordance with the principles of autonomy and assistance tasks with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia. 3. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region. 4. Mayor is the Mayor of Bukittinggi. 5. Regional House of Representatives of the City of Bukittinggi, hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD, is a regional people's representative institution as an element of regional government administration. 6. Regional Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is a unit that has authority in the field of women's empowerment and family planning. 7. Community is individuals, families, groups and social organizations and/or community organizations. 8. Customs are permanent patterns of behavior passed down from one generation to another as heritage so that they are strongly integrated with community behavior patterns. 9. Non-Governmental Organization, hereinafter abbreviated as LSM, is an organization/institution formed by citizens of the Republic of Indonesia voluntarily of their own accord and interested in and engaged in the field of social welfare as a manifestation of community participation in improving the standard of living and welfare of the community with emphasis on voluntary service. 10. Social Organization is an institution/foundation/social association formed by the community, whether legally established or not, which functions as a means of community participation in carrying out social welfare activities. 11. Empowerment is a process, method and act of providing power and strength so that a person is able to explore potential and positive energy and have an impact on a better quality of life. 12. Woman is every person who is born, recognized by society and registered as a woman. 13. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of women so that they can live healthily, develop themselves and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or post-remedial (assistance and treatment) protection. 14. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including children still in the womb. 15. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination. 16. q. To receive protection from being targets of persecution, torture or imposition of inhumane punishment or sanctions.
r. To obtain freedom in accordance with the law. s. Every child deprived of their liberty has the right to: 1. receive humane treatment and be placed separately from adults;
2. receive legal assistance or other assistance effectively at every stage of applicable legal remedies; and
3. defend themselves and obtain justice before an objective and impartial juvenile court in a closed hearing.
t. Every child who becomes a victim or perpetrator of sexual violence or who is in conflict with the law has the right to confidentiality.
u. To receive legal assistance and other assistance if they become a victim or perpetrator of a criminal act.
